models.name: FLUX.1 schnell (GGUF)
models.description: Fast 12B rectified-flow text-to-image model, Apache-2.0. Quantized weights for modest VRAM; needs the CLIP-L and T5-XXL encoders and the FLUX autoencoder.

components.label: Diffusion model
components.description: Quantized FLUX.1 schnell weights.

components.label: T5-XXL text encoder

models.name: FLUX.1 schnell (single file)

components.label: Checkpoint

models.name: FLUX.2 klein 4B

components.label: Diffusion model
components.description: Q8_0 is the quality reference; Q4_0 roughly halves the footprint.

components.label: FLUX.2 autoencoder
components.description: Shared across the FLUX.2 family. Gated: accept the licence and set HF_TOKEN.

components.label: Qwen3-4B text encoder
components.description: Q4_0 is ample for prompt encoding.

models.name: FLUX.2 klein 9B
models.description: Distilled 9B FLUX.2 model for text-to-image and reference-image editing, four steps at cfg 1. Noticeably better detail and prompt adherence than klein 4B for roughly twice the memory. FLUX non-commercial licence; the autoencoder comes from the gated FLUX.2-dev repository, so installing this one needs HF_TOKEN.

components.label: Diffusion model

components.label: FLUX.2 autoencoder

components.label: Qwen3-8B text encoder

models.name: Z-Image Turbo
models.description: Tongyi's distilled 6B text-to-image model, eight steps at CFG 1, with strong photorealism and bilingual text rendering. On a 24 GB GPU run the bf16 weights with a Q8_0 or bf16 text encoder: the Q4 encoders used on smaller cards visibly flatten detail. Its output is soft at 1 MP by design, so the default adds a 1.5x hires detail pass (4x-UltraSharp, then 8 steps at 0.3 denoise) for crisp skin, hair and texture. Apache-2.0, ungated.

components.label: Diffusion model
components.description: bf16 is the reference; Q8_0 and int8 convrot are near-lossless at half the size. Q4 and below lose fine detail.

components.label: FLUX.1 autoencoder
components.description: Z-Image decodes with the FLUX.1 autoencoder (ae.safetensors). This is Comfy-Org's ungated copy, byte-for-byte the one in the gated FLUX.1-schnell repo. Not the diffusers-format vae/diffusion_pytorch_model.safetensors, which stable-diffusion.cpp cannot load as this model's VAE.

components.label: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 text encoder
components.description: Q8_0 or F16 on 24 GB. Q4 encoders cost prompt adherence and fine detail for 2 GB of savings.

models.name: Qwen-Image (GGUF)
models.description: 20B MMDiT text-to-image model with unusually strong text rendering, including Chinese. Uses Qwen2.5-VL as its text encoder.

models.name: Qwen-Image 2.1
models.description: Qwen's text-to-image and instruction-editing model, top of the open-weights text-to-image and editing arenas. Qwen3-VL-8B text encoder; transparent PNGs when the prompt asks for an RGBA image; sides must be multiples of 32. On 24 GB run bf16 (14 GB) with a Q8_0 encoder: Q4 quantizations are what produce soft output and faint line artifacts. The default adds a 1.5x hires detail pass, which also removes the faint 8 px striping stable-diffusion.cpp leaves on 1 MP Qwen output. The optional Viggle turbo LoRA samples in 6 steps at CFG 1, applied automatically when selected (without the hires pass, which overcooks turbo output).

components.label: Diffusion model
components.description: bf16 (14 GB) is the reference and fits 24 GB; int8 convrot and Q8_0 are close. Q6_K and below show artifacts.

components.label: Qwen-Image 2.1 autoencoder
components.description: Specific to 2.1: the Qwen-Image and Wan 2.2 VAEs are not interchangeable with it.

components.label: Qwen3-VL-8B text encoder
components.description: Q8_0 for prompt fidelity; Q4_K_M only on small GPUs.

components.label: Qwen3-VL-8B vision projector
components.description: Lets the text encoder see reference images. Needed for editing; not for text-to-image.

components.label: Viggle turbo LoRA (6 steps)
components.description: Six-step distillation at CFG 1: about 4x faster, slightly less detail. Pepper applies its schedule when it is selected.

models.name: LTX-2.5 Distilled (22B)
models.description: Lightricks' 22B audio-video model, distilled to 8 steps at CFG 1: synchronized video and sound in one pass, the cheapest route to 720p on a 24 GB GPU. Renders at 640x352, then the x2 latent spatial upscaler and a short refine pass bring it to 1280x704 (hires). Frame counts are 8k+1 (121 = 5 s at 24 fps). LTX-2.x Community License: free for organizations under $10M revenue. Files come from comfyicu/LTX-2.5, an ungated copy of the official Lightricks/LTX-2.5 repo, which requires accepting the licence and an HF token.

components.label: Diffusion model
components.description: Q6_K (18.6 GB) is the largest that leaves room for activations on 24 GB; Q8_0 needs more VRAM.

components.label: Gemma 4 12B text encoder (LTX-2.5)

components.label: Video VAE (conv)

components.label: Audio VAE

components.label: Latent spatial upscaler x2

models.name: Wan 2.2 T2V A14B
models.description: Alibaba's 14B mixture-of-experts text-to-video model, the open-weights leader for photoreal people and camera motion. Two experts (high-noise and low-noise) sample in turn. Ships with the lightx2v Lightning LoRA pair, on by default: 4 steps at CFG 1, about 10x faster; send loras: [] for the full 20-step model. 832x480 at 16 fps, 81 frames; finish with a SeedVR2 upscale for 1080p. Apache-2.0.

Qwen2.5-VL-7B and a ByT5 glyph encoder condition it, so it renders on-screen text well. This is the CFG-distilled I2V checkpoint: CFG 1, half the compute. Frame counts are 4k+1. Apache-2.0-style Tencent Hunyuan license.

models.description: General-purpose instruct model with tool calling and a hybrid thinking mode. A good default for an 8-16GB GPU.

models.name: SmolLM3 3B
models.description: Compact multilingual instruct model. Small enough to run on CPU at usable speed, which makes it a good first install.

models.name: Chatterbox TTS
models.description: Expressive text-to-speech with zero-shot voice cloning from a short reference clip, plus emotion exaggeration control.

models.name: Qwen3-TTS VoiceDesign 1.7B

models.name: VibeVoice 1.5B

models.name: Qwen3-ASR 0.6B

models.name: ACE-Step 1.5 Turbo
models.description: Full songs with vocals or instrumentals from a style prompt and lyrics ([Verse]/[Chorus] markers), 50+ languages, in seconds: the fastest open music model, with cover, repaint and continuation routes. MIT license, commercial use allowed.

models.name: HeartMuLa
models.description: A music language model for complete songs from lyrics and comma-separated style tags, with the strongest lyric control among open models and multilingual singing. Slower than ACE-Step. Apache-2.0.

models.name: YuE2 3B
models.description: m-a-p's song model: plans melody and chords from the style and lyrics, then sings and arranges full 48 kHz stereo songs of several minutes (English and Mandarin). Tops SongBench among open models, above ACE-Step 1.5 and Suno v5; a 3.6-minute song takes about 70 s in 11 GB on a 4090. Runs in its own Python environment, built on first use. CC BY-NC 4.0: non-commercial use only.
